credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}} even as depreciation, amortisation and impairment grew by {{dda.change@FY2025}}.

Total debt was reduced by {{total_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{total_debt@FY2025}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{net_debt@FY2025}}, taking gross leverage down by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}.
Interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2025}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2025}} as finance costs fell by {{finance_costs.change@FY2025}} to {{finance_costs@FY2025}}.
FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, lifting FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}.

Free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} as capex rose by {{capex.change@FY2025}} to {{capex@FY2025}}, although FCF to debt still improved by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} on the smaller debt base.

liquidity_funding.text: Liquidity fell by {{liquidity.change@FY2025}} to {{liquidity@FY2025}}, of which cash and cash-like investments declined by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}.
Undrawn committed facilities fell by {{undrawn_facilities.change@FY2025}} to {{undrawn_facilities@FY2025}}, so the buffer outside cash narrowed as well.

Liquidity to revenue fell by {{liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, and cash liquidity to revenue by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.

Advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} while contract liabilities declined by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}}, so a larger share of the cash base is customer prepayments.

operating_performance.text: Capacity grew by {{ask.change@FY2025}} to {{ask@FY2025}} available seat kilometres, while traffic was broadly unchanged, with RPK up {{rpk.change@FY2025}} to {{rpk@FY2025}} and passengers stable at {{passengers@FY2025}}.
Unit revenue improved: RASK rose by {{rask.change@FY2025}} to {{rask@FY2025}} and passenger yield by {{passenger_yield.change@FY2025}} to {{passenger_yield@FY2025}}.

CASK fell by {{cask.change@FY2025}} to {{cask@FY2025}}, but CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2025}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2025}} as fuel cost declined by {{fuel_cost.change@FY2025}} to {{fuel_cost@FY2025}} and its share of costs eased by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2025}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}}.

The fleet grew by {{fleet.change@FY2025}} to {{fleet@FY2025}} aircraft at an average age of {{fleet_age@FY2025}}, broadly unchanged, with engine availability constraining British Airways' Middle East schedule.

peer_positioning.text: IAG leads the network airlines on leverage and cash generation, with the lowest net leverage ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}) and gross leverage ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}) and the highest FFO to debt ({{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2025}}).

Its EBITDA margin of {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} is the highest of the group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2025}}), well above the peer median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2025}}, and interest coverage of {{interest_coverage@FY2025}} also ranks first ({{interest_coverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}).

The weakest point is customer prepayment cover, where advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is the highest of the group ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@FY2025}}) against a peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@FY2025}}, while capex intensity and cash liquidity to revenue sit in the middle of the group.

snapshot.text: International Airlines Group, the owner of British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025, a year in which industrial action and supply-chain constraints disrupted operations.

The EBITDA margin widened by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} and net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}}, the lowest of the network peers.
The point to watch is liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} as cash was returned to shareholders.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, in line with the peer median but weaker than a year earlier.

Cash returns: the group announced a share buyback and a further return of excess cash, which will keep drawing on the cash base that already fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}.

Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@FY2025}} and the highest of the group, a sensitivity if bookings slow.
Unit cost: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2025}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2025}}, so the improvement in total unit cost rests on the lower fuel bill.
